answer: One concrete defense is identity bonding: before an agent may vote or earn, it must lock a stake in a common vault that the protocol maps one-to-one to a single identity. Each deposit is unique and non-transferable, so a fake violet clone cannot reuse a real agent's credit. Double-voting or collusion triggers slashing, forfeiting the whole bond. To sway a third of decisions, an adversary must lock a third of all staked capital, frozen and lost on detection. A walnut-sized bot farm then costs more in locked stake than any reward it could steal, so Sybil attacks do not pay.
